assessments.reasoning: The dated and approved SDC field note names Jules I. Schwartz and repeats its report number in page headers. The title has an open-publication restriction, and its introduction identifies the same-date interpreter scope. The fresh PDF hash and every associated raw page, image and content object range match. The cited physical pages were rerendered and inspected at 139 dpi. The displayed passage at FN-LO-34-2, §1.1 Remarks on Symbology mapping, printed p. 4 / PDF p. 4; §6.1 Properties of Statements, item (2), printed p. 19 / PDF p. 19 addresses the proposition. The visual hardware-to-true-symbol table in §1.1 maps a lone dollar sign to a semicolon. Section 6.1 limits its discussion to simple statements and item (2) requires the hardware notation's dollar terminator. The assessment stays within the named dated SDC document and its scope. It assesses documentary wording, not execution on a specific implementation. The hardware table also lists separate paired characters with embedded dollar signs. Section 9 uses BEGIN and END to bracket compounds and does not put a dollar after each closing END in the shown example. The exact proposition covers simple statement termination in the 1960 keypunch representation.

challenge.method: Inspect the symbol table and the complete §6.1 note together. Test the tempting broader readings that each dollar sign ends a statement and that the rule also requires a trailing dollar after compound END.
challenge.results: The hardware table also lists separate paired characters with embedded dollar signs. Section 9 uses BEGIN and END to bracket compounds and does not put a dollar after each closing END in the shown example. The exact proposition covers simple statement termination in the 1960 keypunch representation.

limitations: This claim concerns the February 1, 1960 field note and its described profile.
The rule concerns simple statements and the edition’s keypunch representation. Uses of the character in composite tokens and accepted spellings in later implementations are separate questions.
The mapping describes that edition's notation. It does not establish input accepted by any current parser or later dialect.
